title: Grammar: Build the imparfait for past habits and descriptions
subtitle: A2 · Unit 4: Tell a clear story

steps.title: Build the imparfait for past habits and descriptions
steps.body: A clear past account often needs two jobs: describe the background or a repeated habit, then report a completed event. Use the imparfait for the first job and the passé composé forms already learned in Units 2 and 3 for the second.

steps.title: Use the nous present stem without -ons, then add -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Être uses ét-.
rows: I / she / we used to take
I / we used to go home
I / she used to meet up

steps.title: Build the imparfait for past habits and descriptions
steps.body:
• Most imparfait forms start from the present nous form: nous parlons → parl-, then add the ending.
• Être is the main exception: its stem is ét- (j'étais, nous étions).
• Use it for a repeated past habit (chaque matin, je prenais le bus) or a description (la salle était calme).
• The endings -ais, -ait, and -aient usually sound alike; use the subject to choose the spelling.
• In your notes, write the stem and ending separately, then close the notes and rebuild one sentence from memory.

steps.prompt: Quand j'étais jeune, nous ___ près du centre.
steps.explain: A repeated past living situation uses the imparfait: nous habitions.

steps.prompt: Chaque hiver, il ___ froid le matin.
steps.explain: A repeated past weather condition uses il faisait.

steps.prompt: Choose the imparfait form of avoir with elle.
steps.explain: The imparfait form is elle avait.

steps.prompt: Complete: La pièce ___ une grande fenêtre.
